Viral Fever – Public Health Reference
Overview
Viral fever is a general term for fever caused by viruses... It usually improves within a few days with rest and fluids. Some serious illnesses such as dengue, malaria or bacterial infections can also start with fever, so persistent or severe symptoms need medical evaluation.
Common Symptoms
Fever, chills, headache, body ache, tiredness, sore throat, cough, runny nose, loss of appetite, mild nausea. Symptoms vary depending on the virus.
Causes
Spread through droplets, close contact, contaminated hands/surfaces, or by mosquitoes for some viral diseases. Seasonal changes can increase circulation of viruses.
When to See a Doctor
Seek medical care urgently for: difficulty breathing; confusion; persistent high fever; fever lasting more than 2–3 days or returning; severe dehydration; repeated vomiting; severe abdominal pain; seizures; rash with bleeding; pregnancy, infants, older adults, or people with serious illness developing fever.
Home Care and Prevention
Rest well, drink plenty of safe fluids, eat light nutritious food, maintain hand hygiene, cover coughs/sneezes, avoid close contact while sick, use safe drinking water and mosquito control where appropriate, and follow medical advice.
Odisha-specific notes
In Odisha, viral and mosquito-borne fevers commonly increase during the monsoon because of standing water and higher mosquito breeding. During summer, dehydration and heat can occur along with seasonal viral illnesses. Any fever during these seasons should be monitored carefully because dengue, chikungunya and malaria may have similar early symptoms.
Source basis
Prepared by paraphrasing general public health guidance from WHO, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (India), ICMR, National Health Mission, National Centre for Disease Control, and Odisha Health & Family Welfare Department.

This content is for general awareness only and does not replace professional medical advice.
